introHeading: The roaming booth for Queens' biggest guest lists
introParas: Queens throws some of the biggest guest lists we see all year — multigenerational weddings and Sweet Sixteens that fill an entire catering hall in Astoria, Flushing or Forest Hills. At that scale, a single static booth with one line running all night leaves a lot of the room uncovered. The roaming photo booth solves it differently: an attendant carries a handheld, lit capture system table to table, so guests get photographed wherever they're sitting instead of queuing across a crowded hall.

Sessions take under a minute — the attendant approaches a table, the group picks stills, GIFs or boomerangs, and the photo lands on their phone by text or email on the spot. Because there's no booth to place, there's no footprint to plan around, no dedicated power run and no backdrop to fit into an already-packed catering hall floor plan. For the biggest weddings, we usually pair the roamer with the mirror or vogue booth: the static booth anchors one corner and draws the crowd that wants to line up for it, while the roamer covers the tables, the bar and the cocktail hour before dinner is even served.

It's also a strong fit for Long Island City corporate parties and trade show-style events, where guests are circulating rather than queuing. Queens is a standard service area with no surprise travel fees — we quote it from your venue ZIP code before you book, so nothing shows up on the invoice that wasn't in the quote.

faqHeading: Roaming Photo Booth in Queens — FAQ

faqs.q: How much space does the roaming booth need at a Queens catering hall?
faqs.a: None. There's no footprint to plan around, which is why it's a common add-on for catering halls in Astoria, Flushing and Forest Hills that are already packed with tables.

faqs.q: Our guest list is large — is the roaming booth enough on its own?
faqs.a: For a catering hall running 200-plus guests, we usually recommend pairing it with the mirror or vogue booth. The static booth draws the crowd that wants to line up for it, while the roamer covers the tables and cocktail hour so coverage stays high across the whole room.

faqs.q: Do you charge a travel fee in Queens?
faqs.a: Queens is a standard service area with no surprise fees. We quote it from your venue ZIP code before you book.

faqs.q: What kind of Queens venues have you worked the roaming booth in?
faqs.a: Large catering halls in Astoria, Flushing and Forest Hills, plus corporate parties in Long Island City lofts. Send us your venue name on the quote form and we'll tell you exactly what fits.

faqs.q: Does the roaming booth need power at the venue?
faqs.a: No. The handheld capture system needs no dedicated outlet, which matters at a catering hall where every outlet is already spoken for by the DJ and catering staff.

faqs.q: Does the roaming booth print photos?
faqs.a: It's digital-first — photos go straight to guests' phones by text or email. Pair it with a static booth and printer station if you want prints too.

faqs.q: Is an attendant included with the roaming booth rental?
faqs.a: Yes. A trained attendant carries the capture system table to table for the full length of your rental, keeping coverage moving through a large room.

faqs.q: Do you carry insurance and can you provide a COI for our venue?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $2 million insurance policy. If your Queens venue needs a certificate of insurance naming them as additionally insured, reply to your booking confirmation with their contact email and we'll send it over.
